text:
Charle-Edouard D'Astous went undrafted, played in Finland and Sweden, and reached the NHL at 27. In his second season with Tampa Bay, he is suddenly one of the Lightning's most productive defensemen: 13 points in 19 games, 7 of them on the power play, and about 20 minutes a night over his last ten games, up more than four from last season.

Some of this is the role. More power-play time means more assists, and most of his points are assists. Some of it is luck. His scoring rate is well above the top of our talent range for him, and teammates have scored about four goals more than their chances with him on the ice, the kind of finishing that tends to fade.

The underlying game gives the bump some support. At five-on-five, Tampa Bay has had about 57% of the chance quality with him out there. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 86th percentile among defensemen at driving play last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving his own zone with the puck on 60% of his exits. What we'd watch is whether the minutes stay when the points slow.
headline: Charle-Edouard D'Astous has earned a bigger job
